residual_risks: Records that were already IN_APPROVAL when p9_014 deployed keep `approval_chain_snapshot IS NULL`. For those rows the chain still derives from the live matrix (documented as intentional in the p9_014 docstring) AND the new per-step `submitted_by` self-review assertion never fires — the mid-flight-rebind / self-approval hole the committee asked to close therefore remains open for exactly those rows. The migration docstring declares the NULL chain fallback, but the loss of the self-review guard for legacy rows is not stated anywhere in the change.

The one-success-one-reject guarantee for concurrent submit / approval-step rests entirely on the PostgreSQL `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` row lock (with `populate_existing`); the reviewed test file states that the in-memory SQLite fixture (StaticPool, shared connection) cannot express concurrency, so no test in this batch observes the serialized behaviour. The lock path itself reads correctly on inspection (the record row is the only exclusively locked relation, and the re-read picks up the committed approval_step / approval_role), but it is unverified by the reviewed tests.

`alembic check` was not executed against a live schema in this review. I did verify the p9_014 table list against ORM metadata programmatically: the migration's 20 tables are exactly the RecordMixin consumers (`streams` is correctly excluded because it declares approval_step/approval_depth without inheriting RecordMixin), and `REQUIRED_WORKFLOW_COLUMNS` is derived from `RecordMixin.__annotations__`, so it now automatically requires `approval_chain_snapshot` — no registry model can pass the workflow-column guard without the new column. The actual DB state of `pcs` / `pcs_test` remains unverified.

`submit_approval` reads the project's RECORD matrix binding *after* taking the record row lock, but the binding read itself is not locked. A rebind that commits between that read and the snapshot write leaves the snapshot holding the pre-rebind chain while the project already points at the new matrix. That is consistent with the intended "freeze at submit" semantics, but it means the frozen chain of a record submitted at time T depends on a read that is not atomic with the binding change.
testing_gaps: No test asserts that exactly one `record-actions-error` node exists after the reason modal is closed following a failed action; the new test added in this batch (tests/components/common/RecordActions.test.tsx) only covers the modal-open state, which is the one state where the duplicate cannot occur.

No frontend test clicks 查询 while the audit table is on a page other than 1 (the `setPage(1)` -> pagination-effect path that must pick up the newly applied filter). The two `audit-filter-submit` clicks in tests/pages/audit/AuditLogPage.export.test.tsx (lines 333, 383) both exercise the page===1 direct-query path, so the effect-driven path that pairs `setAppliedFilter` with `setPage(1)` is unverified.

No backend test covers the `approval_chain_snapshot IS NULL` fallback (a record already IN_APPROVAL at deploy time derives its chain from the live matrix) nor the absence of the per-step `submitted_by` self-review assertion for such rows; the new tests in tests/api/v1/test_record_approval_chain.py all submit first, so the snapshot is always present.

No test asserts that a project insert failing on a constraint other than `uq_projects_project_no` is *not* reported as `PROJECT_NO_CONFLICT`; tests/api/v1/test_project_creation.py only covers the genuine duplicate.

Verified: projects.project_no carries a real DB unique constraint (alembic dd47298c9c38, uq_projects_project_no), and every other NOT NULL column on the projects row is supplied by ProjectCreate (project_name / owner_company / location / project_type / design_phase / unit_system / workspace_id all min_length=1; product_category is a ProductCategory enum whose 3 members match the ck_projects_product_category CHECK exactly), so the only other reachable integrity failure is an fk_projects_workspace_id violation if the workspace is deleted between the existence check and the INSERT. FORMAL workspaces have retention_days=None (no TTL sweep), so that race is narrow — but when it does fire, the API tells the user their project number is taken, and changing the number does not help. Narrowing the catch to the constraint name would remove the misleading message.

create_project's `await db.rollback()` in the IntegrityError branch is safe here: it is reached with exactly one pending object (the Project row just added), so there is no caller work to destroy, and get_db rolls the (already-rolled-back) session back again on the raised PcsError (app/db/session.py:123-126).

The new approval_chain_snapshot column is NOT exposed anywhere: it appears only in app/models/mixins.py:77 and app/api/v1/records_actions.py; it is absent from app/schemas/*, pcs-backend/docs/openapi.json, pcs-frontend/openapi.snapshot.json, and pcs-frontend/src/types/api.d.ts. The project binding read face (app/api/v1/signature_matrices.py:223, ProjectMatrixBindingOut) returns the LIVE matrix steps, never the snapshot, so submitted_by / submitted_by_role cannot leak through it. No endpoint echoes a record row wholesale (app/api/v1/records.py builds explicit 5-field dicts). The only CSV export in the batch is the audit-log export (pcs-frontend/src/pages/audit/AuditLogPage.tsx), which exports audit columns only.

The sibling approval path (change notices / deliverables) still honours the matrix's can_self_check, which the builtin templates never set and parse_steps defaults to True (app/services/signature_matrix_service.py:187, app/services/deliverable_service.py:879) — so a change-notice submitter may sign their own version. That path is untouched by this diff (pre-existing) and the committee's freeze-the-chain ruling was applied only to the record side; flagging it here only as the same class of hole one module over.

The submit-time self-review check compares the single JWT role (actor.role), while the per-step check compares user_id. The per-step check is the stronger of the two and dominates every case I could construct (a user holding several roles, or re-authenticating under a different role, is still caught by user_id), so the role-based submit-time check is only an early-out. actor.user_id is derived deterministically from the JWT sub/user_id claim (app/api/v1/config.py:533-540) and is stable across login and refresh, so the identity used for submitted_by cannot drift between the submit and the approval request.
testing_gaps: The row locks this batch added to both write paths are only effective on PostgreSQL — SQLite silently drops FOR UPDATE, and the repo's only test database is in-memory SQLite (CLAUDE.md: 'tests/conftest.py 用 sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory: + SA_Base.metadata.create_all'). The test file states the gap itself: '本仓单测的 in-memory SQLite 走 StaticPool —— 两个请求共享同一条连接/同一个事务域，根本没有隔离 ⇒ 真并发在本 fixture 上不可表达 ... FOR UPDATE 行锁（SQLite 方言静默省略）在 PG 上把并发提交串行化 ... CI 的 fresh-PG api-drift job 负责那条链路'. I found no PostgreSQL-backed test in the repo (no pg marker in pyproject.toml / conftest.py), so the concurrent-double-submit and concurrent-double-approval-step serialisation — the property the FOR UPDATE + populate_existing pair exists to provide, and the reason ADR-0047's '不重不漏' audit claim depends on it — is currently unverified by any automated test.

No test exercises the approval_chain_snapshot IS NULL branch of approval_step (the legacy-row fallback). The added tests in tests/api/v1/test_record_approval_chain.py only cover the snapshot-present path (test_submit_persists_chain_snapshot, test_midflight_rebind_cannot_change_pending_role, test_matrix_disabled_mid_approval_keeps_chain). A regression test that seeds an IN_APPROVAL record with approval_chain_snapshot = None would pin the behaviour of the fallback and of whatever fix is applied to it.

No test asserts that the snapshot's submitted_by / submitted_by_role stay out of every response body — the protection is currently implicit (the column simply is not in any schema). A single schema-level assertion (e.g. asserting the record read endpoints' JSON has no 'approval_chain_snapshot' key) would catch a future 'return the ORM row wholesale' change.

findings.title: Row-lock concurrency guarantee asserted but verified nowhere
findings.suggested_fix: Two complementary pieces, both reachable from the diff. (1) Pin the *mechanism* with a dialect-level unit test that needs no PG server: compile the lock statement against the PostgreSQL dialect and assert the emitted SQL contains `FOR UPDATE`, e.g. `assert 'FOR UPDATE' in str(select(PipingResult).where(PipingResult.pipe_id == pk).with_for_update().compile(dialect=postgresql.dialect()))` — this fails loudly if the `.with_for_update()` call is dropped or mistyped, and is exactly the shape the repo already uses to guard migrations. (2) Fix the false delegation in `tests/api/v1/test_record_approval_chain.py:444-446`: it claims "CI 的 fresh-PG api-drift job 负责那条链路", but that job runs no backend test at all, so the sentence must either be replaced with a pointer to a real PG-only concurrency test, or the test must actually be added. For (2), model the new test on the repo's existing isolated-schema subprocess pattern in `tests/alembic/test_p9_013_bind_default_record_matrix.py` (create a throwaway PG schema, then drive two independent connections/sessions at the same record row and assert exactly one 200 and one 409 `SIGNATURE_MATRIX_NOT_ACTIVE`/state-machine 409). Assumption stated: adding a PG-gated test is acceptable for this repo — the isolation helpers already exist there, and the alternative (a real PG service in CI) is a larger decision. Note the repo already has the in-repo precedent for exactly this shape of concern: `app/services/advisory_lock.py` (bug-119) implements a dialect-aware fail-fast — SQLite → silent no-op, PostgreSQL → re-raise — so a lock that is inert on SQLite is a known, already-categorised hazard here; `load_record(for_update=True)` is the one lock site that has no dialect-aware guard and no test at all.

findings.title: p9_014 table list never cross-checked against ORM
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test that derives the expected table set from the ORM instead of trusting the literal, and asserts the migration's list equals it. The ORM metadata already carries the column on exactly the right tables (`deliverables` and `streams` do not inherit `RecordMixin`, so they do not have it), so the comparison is exact: import `app.models` for side effects, then `from app.db.base import Base`; assert `set(module._TABLES) == {t.name for t in Base.metadata.tables.values() if 'approval_chain_snapshot' in t.columns}`. Put it next to the existing `tests/alembic/test_p9_013_bind_default_record_matrix.py` shape assertions, and extend the roundtrip test's `information_schema` probe from the single `flash_results` table to the whole `_TABLES` tuple so a missing column on any of the 20 tables is caught on a real engine. The same guard makes the migration's docstring claim ("与 ORM 元数据一致") an enforced invariant instead of an assertion in prose.

findings.title: No backfill: in-flight records keep the unbinding hole open
findings.suggested_fix: Bound the exposure explicitly, in two parts. (a) Back-fill the *chain* half of the snapshot in `p9_014.upgrade()` for rows already `IN_APPROVAL`, deriving `matrix_id`/`steps` from the project's currently bound RECORD matrix — the chain is recoverable; the submitter identity is not (there is no submitter column on the record), so `submitted_by` should be left absent rather than faked, and `approval_step`'s existing `if snapshot and snapshot.get("submitted_by") == ...` guard already degrades correctly when the key is missing. (b) Add a test that drives a record whose `approval_chain_snapshot` is explicitly NULL through `approval-step` and asserts the live-matrix fallback still advances the chain (and that the chain is *not* frozen for that row), so the compatibility branch is pinned rather than accidental. Assumption stated: (a) assumes pre-deploy `IN_APPROVAL` rows are worth a data migration; if the project is genuinely empty in that state, the cheaper alternative is to drop the fallback branch's tolerance and make a NULL snapshot a loud 409 instead of a silent downgrade to the live matrix.

findings.title: A-3 label lookup drops runtime fallback, crashes on unknown type
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the compile-time exhaustiveness of `Record<WorkflowType, {tab, section}>` but restore runtime tolerance at the lookup site: `const label = WORKFLOW_LABELS[section.workflow_type]?.section ?? section.workflow_type;`. If the project's ESLint config enables `@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-condition` (which would flag the optional chain on a non-optional index type), expose a helper in `workflowTabs.ts` instead — e.g. `export function workflowLabel(type: string): string { return (WORKFLOW_LABELS as Partial<Record<WorkflowType, {tab: string; section: string}>>)[type as WorkflowType]?.section ?? type; }` — so the map stays exhaustive for the compiler while the lookup tolerates an unknown runtime key. Add one unit test that renders `SectionBlock` with an out-of-vocabulary `workflow_type` and asserts the raw key is displayed rather than the component throwing.

residual_risks: The `FOR UPDATE` guarantee is argued from PostgreSQL READ-COMMITTED semantics (a blocked `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` re-reads the newly committed row version) and from `populate_existing` defeating the identity map. Neither was executed or observed on a real PostgreSQL in this review; if `populate_existing` were dropped from the `execution_options` call the identity map could serve a stale `approval_step` after the lock wait, and nothing in the suite would notice. See the P1 finding.

Absence claims in this review rest on text/grep search over `tests/`, `scripts/`, and `.github/workflows/` (the code-review-graph MCP server was unreachable this session, so no symbol-aware references were available). A concurrency or table-drift check living in an unsearched location would weaken the two P1/P2 findings.

`create_project`'s `except IntegrityError` handler maps *every* integrity violation to `PROJECT_NO_CONFLICT` ("项目编号 … 已存在"). Today `project_no` is the only unique constraint on `Project` (`app/models/project.py:54`), so the mapping is currently correct, but any future NOT NULL / FK / check violation on `Project` would surface to the user as a false "duplicate project number" 409.

`submit_approval` writes `record.approval_chain_snapshot` *before* the `_transition` call that can reject the submit with 409, so the rejected request leaves a mutated record in the session. This is safe today only because the production dependency `get_db` rolls back on exception and the test override's `async with factory() as session` closes (and therefore rolls back) the session when the endpoint raises. A future change that commits or reuses the session after a caught `PcsError` would persist the rejected submitter's snapshot.

The frontend `errorText` unification changed `DeliverableSignDialog`'s error prefix separator from ASCII `:` to the fullwidth `：` used by `DeliverableProgressPage`. Display-only, but it changes user-visible text for the deliverable sign dialog and no test pins either delimiter on that dialog.

The deliverable-progress page's `workflow_type` narrowing to the three-value `WorkflowType` union is an unchecked runtime assertion on an API response whose OpenAPI contract is a bare `string`; it is currently safe only because the backing PostgreSQL column is a native enum constrained to those three members.
testing_gaps: No test exercises the snapshot-less (legacy `approval_chain_snapshot IS NULL`) compatibility branch of `_next_approval_role` — every approval test in `tests/api/v1/test_record_approval_chain.py` and `tests/api/v1/test_records_actions_statemachine.py` obtains its snapshot by calling `submit-approval` first.

No test drives two concurrent requests against one record row on a real PostgreSQL, so the `FOR UPDATE` serialisation of `submit-approval` and `approval-step` — and the "exactly one `APPROVAL_STEP_PASSED` audit row" claim in the code comment — are asserted only in prose. The repo already has the pattern for this (`tests/alembic/test_p9_013_bind_default_record_matrix.py` reaches a real PG through an isolated schema) but never applied it to a concurrency case.

No test compares `p9_014._TABLES` with the ORM's `RecordMixin` leaf tables, so a table added to the ORM without a matching migration entry fails nothing; the PG roundtrip test's `information_schema` probe covers `flash_results` only.

No test pins the SQL emitted by `load_record(for_update=True)` under the PostgreSQL dialect, so removing or mistyping `.with_for_update()` is invisible to the suite (SQLite silently omits the clause).

No test covers the `SIGNATURE_MATRIX_EMPTY_CHAIN` branch when the matrix row is deleted between submit and the next approval step — the frozen snapshot should keep the chain alive, but the deleted-matrix path is only exercised for the *disabled* matrix, not the *missing* one.

No test asserts that `submit-approval` leaves the record's `approval_chain_snapshot` untouched when the request is rejected (self-review 403 / already-in-approval 409); the existing `test_second_submit_after_commit_is_409` checks the persisted value only after a `refresh`, which would also pass if the rejection path mutated the session object.
